EXPERIMENT 07
Android Forensics Acquisition and AFLogical Extraction
Objective

To perform mobile device forensic acquisition of an Android handset using the Android Debug Bridge (ADB) and the AFLogical OSE forensic application, retrieve communication and contact artifacts, pull extracted forensic data to the analysis workstation, and verify evidence integrity via cryptographic hashing.

Tools / Requirements
  • Forensic Utilities: Android Debug Bridge (adb Version 1.0.41), AFLogical OSE (aflogical-ose.apk)
  • Workstation Environment: Microsoft Windows 11 Home / Windows PowerShell
  • Mobile Device Target: Android Handset (Device Identifier: 41311JEHN05115)
  • Connection Interface: USB Debugging with RSA Host Key Authorization
Experiment Scenario
Controlled laboratory evidence was used for this experiment.

A mobile digital forensics acquisition scenario was conducted on an Android device connected to a Windows analysis workstation. The investigator established ADB connectivity, verified authorization credentials, deployed the AFLogical OSE forensic agent, extracted logical evidence containers (call logs, contacts, SMS messages), retrieved the artifact bundle via adb pull, and validated the exported forensic dataset with SHA-256 hashing.

Evidence / Input
  • Target Device Serial: 41311JEHN05115 (Android Handset)
  • Evidence Output Directory on Device: /sdcard/forensics/20260919_101230
  • Extracted Evidence Bundle: CallLog_Calls.csv (12.4 KB), Contacts_Phones.csv (28.7 KB), SMS.csv (14.9 KB), MMS.csv, info.xml
  • Host Destination Directory: C:\Users\sekhar\DIGITAL-FORENSICS\EXP-07\evidence\20260919_101230
Procedure
Step 1 — ADB Installation Check and Device Authorization State

The Android Debug Bridge was initialized on the workstation. Initial device connection returned an unauthorized status, indicating the mobile handset required interactive user trust authorization.

Figure 7.1: ADB installation check and unauthorized device response
Step 2 — ADB Device Enumeration After Authorization

The RSA key exchange was accepted on the handset. Running adb devices confirmed the target device 41311JEHN05115 was authorized and ready for logical forensic acquisition.

Figure 7.2: ADB device enumeration after handset authorization
Step 3 — AFLogical OSE Installation and Category Selection

The AFLogical OSE acquisition package was installed onto the target handset. The examiner selected target data categories: CallLogs, Contacts Phones, and SMS.

Figure 7.3: AFLogical OSE app installed and data categories selected
Step 4 — Extraction Completion and On-Device Storage

The extraction routine executed across Android content providers. The application reported successful extraction to /sdcard/forensics/20260919_101230.

Figure 7.4: Extraction complete confirmation dialog on device
Step 5 — Verifying Extracted Files on Mobile Device

On-device storage was inspected under /sdcard/forensics/20260919_101230, verifying structured CSV exports for call logs, contacts, MMS, SMS, and device metadata.

Figure 7.5: Verifying extracted files on mobile device
Step 6 — Pulling Forensic Evidence to Workstation via ADB

The adb pull utility was executed to transfer the extracted forensic folder /sdcard/forensics/20260919_101230 to the local Windows analysis workstation directory.

Figure 7.6: Pulling forensic evidence to workstation via ADB
Step 7 — Reviewing Recovered CSV Communication Records

The retrieved directory was inspected in File Explorer and Microsoft Excel, confirming recovered call logs, phone contact entries, and timestamps.

Figure 7.7: Reviewing recovered CSV communication records
Step 8 — Cryptographic Hash Verification of Extracted Evidence

The PowerShell Get-FileHash command was executed on all extracted CSV and XML evidence files, recording baseline SHA-256 hashes to safeguard the chain of custody.

Figure 7.8: Cryptographic hash verification of extracted evidence
Observations
  1. ADB established communication with the Android device and resolved the authorization state from unauthorized to trusted device.
  2. AFLogical OSE successfully extracted designated content categories without requiring root privileges.
  3. The extracted dataset was saved on the device at /sdcard/forensics/20260919_101230 and pulled via ADB.
  4. Structured CSV evidence files were successfully exported and cataloged on the Windows workstation.
  5. Baseline cryptographic SHA-256 hashes were calculated for each retrieved forensic file.
Findings
  • Logical Acquisition Soundness: AFLogical OSE performed non-invasive logical extraction through standard Android content providers, acquiring sensitive communications while preserving system partition integrity.
  • Evidentiary Chain of Custody: Secure USB debugging transport combined with immediate post-acquisition hashing established verifiable integrity for all recovered mobile phone artifacts.
Conclusion

The AFLogical mobile forensics workflow successfully extracted call history, contacts, SMS records, and device metadata from the Android handset via ADB. The extracted evidence was preserved in structured CSV format and validated with cryptographic hashing.
